runtime_components.component: Pinned NVIDIA CUDA 12.1.1 cuDNN8 devel base

findings: Container license section 1(c) expressly permits compatible derived containers containing the entire base plus software with primary functionality; MuseTalk application functionality is the intended basis, not resale of standalone CUDA.
Retain /NGC-DL-CONTAINER-LICENSE and component notices. Apply section 2 downstream terms; do not blanket-license the entire image as MIT or remove the proprietary terms.
Keep NVIDIA GPU execution scope and no-API-exposure restrictions. If slimming the base or removing components, recheck the grant rather than assuming the entire-base path still applies.
Actual base license bytes must be compared against this reference capture in CI. Source Dockerfile proves the intended path but is not a digest-bound extraction.

runtime_components.component: TensorRT 10.3.0 proprietary wheels versus TensorRT OSS and Torch-TensorRT 2.5.0
runtime_components.basis: Exact wheel SLA plus Apache/BSD notices for separately identified OSS components
findings: Exact cp310 TensorRT bindings wheel license and the 2,037,510,258-byte NVIDIA-hosted libs wheel's license were read (the latter using only 15,891 bytes of HTTP range reads). Both equal the pinned v10.3 packaging license SHA-256 64bd290f0251405f783ba1d2e155c500542be69795e51147a1d9f11a57bda8cc. Its section 12.1 grants binary redistribution of libnvinfer and libnvinfer_plugin as part of a materially functional application with pass-through restrictions.

Current official web SLA instead says runtime .so/.dll files broadly. The old 10.3 archive URL redirects to latest. Do not silently replace packaged terms with latest terms or infer that the whole proprietary wheel is Apache because the GitHub OSS tree is Apache.

The observed normal libs wheel contains libnvinfer.so.10, libnvinfer_plugin.so.10, libnvonnxparser.so.10, libnvinfer_builder_resource.so.10.3.0, and libnvinfer_builder_resource_win.so.10.3.0 (no lean/dispatch files). Resolve scope for the Python binding, parser and builder-resource payload using applicable NVIDIA terms or independently applicable OSS licenses. Obtain release-owner/qualified review or NVIDIA clarification if exact scope remains unresolved. This is a concrete package-term discrepancy, not a conclusion that TensorRT redistribution is categorically forbidden.
Torch-TensorRT is separately BSD-3-Clause; preserve its notice plus TensorRT OSS LICENSE/NOTICE where applicable. Native engine plans retain their model-source provenance obligations.

runtime_components.component: PyAV 16.1.0, Ubuntu FFmpeg, imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0, and OpenCV bundled multimedia libraries
runtime_components.basis: Permissive wrapper licenses plus separate FFmpeg/codec LGPL/GPL/commercial terms
findings: PyAV's own code is BSD-3-Clause and imageio-ffmpeg's wrapper is BSD-2-Clause; neither grants rights for bundled FFmpeg/codecs.

Actual PyAV cp310 manylinux_2_28 wheel metadata/notice entries were inspected via 26373 bytes of HTTP range reads; its wheel-reported BSD license and auditwheel SBOM do not provide a complete FFmpeg codec-license dossier.

The pinned PyAV source references pyav-ffmpeg 8.0.1-3. That build enables x264/x265 and patches them out of FFmpeg's GPL configure list. Do not infer LGPL-only from missing --enable-gpl or a reported license string; require the exact binary source/build/license basis, including any claimed alternate codec grant.

Preserve Ubuntu dpkg copyright files and source-package identities. Provide corresponding FFmpeg/codec source and build scripts by an applicable compliant route; do not rely on a generic upstream link or assume the distributor's source obligation passes to an unrelated host.

Inspect OpenCV and imageio bundled copies separately even if unused at runtime. No --enable-nonfree binary may be treated as freely redistributable. H.264/AAC patent licensing is a separate deployment-specific issue.

runtime_components.component: PyTorch, OpenMMLab and remaining Python/OS dependency graph
runtime_components.basis: Per-component MIT/BSD/Apache and applicable weak/strong copyleft terms
findings: PyTorch and Torch-TensorRT provide BSD-style redistribution grants; MMCV/MMEngine/MMDetection/MMPose are Apache-2.0. Preserve their actual distribution LICENSE/NOTICE and third-party bundled notices, not just root licenses.

Known non-permissive notice/source obligations include certifi MPL-2.0, python-soxr/libsoxr LGPL, SoundFile's bundled libsndfile LGPL, OS GPL/LGPL programs, and optional TTS GPL dependencies. These licenses permit redistribution when their conditions are met; they are not automatic bans.

The constraints file is a superset, not a final SBOM: it contains optional and unused packages. Capture exact installed pip distributions, RECORD-owned native libraries, dpkg binary/source versions, copyright/license files, and build-time source additions from the final image.
